chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Suwayd al-Qalla' from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the man who makes a vow of abstention from his wife.

If he remains for four months and does not return, it is a pronouncement of divorce, then it is suspended. If he returns, it is two divorces in his hand; and if he resolves (to keep it final), it is a final separation from him.

This narration, if taken at its apparent meaning, leads to contradiction with the narrations we presented in the first chapter, that the ruling of divorce and return is only required after the four months. The report implies that this period is a divorce, which is not correct. The correct interpretation is that if he divorces after the four months, it is a revocable divorce. If he returns (meaning he remarries her), it is two divorces in his hand. And if he resolves until the waiting period expires, it becomes a final separation, and he does not have the right to return her except with a new contract and a specified dowry.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal consequence of a husband's vow of abstention (Ila) after four months in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction in this narration by interpreting the 'suspended' status not as a final decree, but as a revocable divorce (Talaq Raj'i) that only becomes irrevocable (Bain) if the husband remains firm until the expiration of the waiting period. This interpretation aligns the report with the broader jurisprudential consensus that the legal ruling is applied after the four-month period, emphasizing the husband's agency in converting the status through his subsequent actions.
